question: Can a fixed conditional recruitment probability g(t) explain different marginal positivity via different observed-duration distributions, and what observable bound could falsify this restricted null?
scope: Analytic selected-observation null, not causal recruitment mechanism, biology fit, force law or a new claim of mathematical novelty.
required_checks: Define eligible observed tracks, positivity denominator and probability distributions
0<=g<=1 common across conditions; total variation convention and bound proved
Sharp baseline-constrained envelope or explicit conceptual limitation, including atoms/zero-support cases
Any binned version explicitly assumes common within-bin positivity, not arbitrary continuous null
Distinguish duration opportunity from endpoint affected by recruitment and selection/censoring/collider bias
Data requirements for positive+negative cohort, independent units, mapping, overlap and uncertainty
Do not infer conditional difference solely from marginal excess under finite empirical noise without valid uncertainty control
Contrast useful falsification criterion with existing unrestricted-selection DASC impossibility
expected_outcomes: Reviewed observable null and falsification envelope
Redundant result with no informative test; stop branch
stop_condition: One independently reviewed bound/design or exact gap. No extended theorem sequence. Hypothetical examples only; no tuning to published summary numbers.
